# EvSidebarItem

> One row of a Sidebar: a destination at main, submenu or sub-submenu depth, or one of the two rows that are not controls - a section heading and a rule.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ID | `evoq-ui:sidebar-item` |
| Layer | Atom (`src/atoms`) |
| Import | `import { EvSidebarItem } from 'evoq-ui'` |
| Template tag | `<EvSidebarItem>` or `<ev-sidebar-item>` |
| Source | `src/atoms/sidebar-item/EvSidebarItem.vue` |
| Extra attributes go to | the root `<li class="ev-sidebar-item--divider">` |
| Used inside | `evoq-ui:sidebar` (EvSidebar) |

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Sidebar**, frame `4446:84476` (Sidebar). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Use as the primary navigation for an app with many sections. Collapse it to icons (Open=No) to reclaim space on desktop; present it as a drawer on mobile.

### When not to use

- Don't use for a handful of top-level destinations — use a top navigation bar. Don't keep the mobile drawer permanently open over content.

### Do

- Group related items under section labels (USER, APPS). Keep the active item clearly highlighted. Preserve icon order between expanded and collapsed states.

### Don't

- Don't nest more than one level of sub-items. Don't hide the collapse control, and don't drop labels in the collapsed state without keeping recognizable icons.

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvSidebarItem`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<li class="ev-sidebar-item--divider">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:sidebar-item` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
